newsitem.title: FRANCE: French public telecom svce costed at 4.8 bln ffr.
newsitem.headline: French public telecom svce costed at 4.8 bln ffr.

text.p: The French telecoms authority ART said on Tuesday that it had estimated the cost of the so-called universal service for telecoms in France at 4.8 billion francs ($812.5 million) in 1997. A final estimate will be made in October.
France Telecom is responsible for providing this universal service and other telecom operators have to contribute to the costs depending on the level of their traffic.
ART said in a statement operators would have to pay 17 centimes per minute to France Telecom, in addition to interconnection charges, for the public service.
Mobile telecoms operators will pay one centime per minute.

ART said that on top of that, some 20 operators would pay six million francs in total to a special fund, managed by the Caisse des Depots et Consignations, which will pay for telephone booths, directories and special discounts for the poor or elderly.
The total costs of these services is estimated at 439 million francs in 1997 and France Telecom pays for the difference.
Full competition in the French telecommunications sector will start in 1998.
A spokesman for ART said that the 1997 cost exercise was a rehearsal for the 1998 figures, for which a first estimate has to be made before September 1997.
